name: Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Ltd (HOEC)
tagline: India's first private E&P company - a chronic B-80 turnaround story that has repeatedly disappointed, now trading at ~100x earnings and a 52-week high on hopes of a ~Rs 1,250 Cr capex programme the forum's own trackers find hard to believe.
business_overview: Small private upstream E&P: producing/discovered fields across Assam (Dirok gas), the Cambay basin, PY-1/PY-3 offshore Cauvery, and the B-80 offshore field (Mumbai offshore, ~60% participating interest). Revenue is oil/gas volumes x price minus a sliding government revenue share + 10% royalty. Seeded via theme-scan 2026-09-09 (user-authorised 1x no-self-discovery bypass), oilfield-services / E&P theme.
fundamentals_table: Volatile; B-80 production has been falling; Dirok evacuation-constrained
fundamentals_narrative: The gap between narrative and delivery is the whole story. B-80 has been 'about to ramp' since 2022 - technical issues, hose repairs, offtake logistics (tankers loaded only when half-full), and production that 'continues to fall' per the June 2026 concall read. Dirok gas is capped by pipeline evacuation (the DNPL captive-line decision and an 18-month wait for the Duliajan Feeder Line). Management now guides ~10,000 boe/d in 2-2.5 years after ~Rs 1,250 Cr capex (~Rs 2,000 Cr/yr revenue), but forum members (#154, #155) call the new CEO's targets 'talk in the air' achievable 'only by merging some company'. ROCE 3.4% fails the quality gate; ~100x earnings at a 52-week high offers no cushion.
technical_read: At the 52-week high (~Rs 193) on the capex-plan narrative and war-driven crude; the operating data (falling B-80 volumes, gated Dirok) does not support it. No weekly/monthly TA pulled - not a Tier-A candidate.
sentiment_summary: topic 1581, 155 posts (2019-2026, category 19). Long arc: 2022 euphoria on B-80 first oil/gas -> 2022-23 disappointment (technical issues, fund-raise, Elango's retirement seen as a big negative) -> 2026 skepticism on the new management's aggressive targets. Recent posts flag the DNPL/DFL evacuation bottleneck (company running at ~1/3 capacity), war-driven crude optionality, and the North East Gas Grid Phase-1 inauguration (March 2026) as the one structural positive. Net tenor: 'unlikely candidate for re-rating - earnings too volatile' (#141).
community_signal: phreakv6 (core trusted) posted #138 in Aug 2023 - a measured, neutral take on Elango's retirement ('shouldn't affect operations since wells are running'); this is an operational observation from three years ago, NOT a current conviction call. vikasbargale (elevated) shared a turnaround-video in May 2024 explicitly 'not invested, just tracking'. No live high-conviction call from any trusted user.
bse_notes: No SEBI/fraud action. Governance is professionally-managed (not promoter-run); long-serving MD Elango retired Aug 2023. New CEO (June 2026) has brought in a team largely from one prior employer, including a CFO who had retired years earlier - flagged as 'odd' by a forum tracker (#154). Aggressive multi-year production targets with thin credibility.
bull_case: Near debt-free; multiple producing/discovered assets (Dirok, B-80, PY-1/PY-3, Cambay)
North East Gas Grid Phase-1 (March 2026) + future Duliajan Feeder Line could eventually unlock Dirok gas volumes
High crude/gas prices improve realisations; gas contracts linked at attractive formulae
If the ~Rs 1,250 Cr capex delivers even half of the 10,000 boe/d target, revenue roughly doubles off a ~Rs 2,550 Cr market cap
bear_case: ROCE ~3.4%, ROE ~2.3% - fails the quality gate; ~100x earnings at a 52-week high
B-80 has disappointed for four straight years; production 'continues to fall'
Dirok gas evacuation-constrained; Duliajan Feeder Line ~18 months out
New management's production targets are viewed as not credible by the forum's own trackers
Commodity price-taker with a sliding government revenue share that rises as revenue rises - caps upside
Earnings too volatile for a re-rating (forum consensus)
verdict_headline: A chronic B-80 turnaround that keeps not turning, evacuation-gated Dirok gas, ROCE ~3.4%, ~100x earnings at a 52-week high, and a new management team whose targets the forum finds not credible. thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (higher crude/gas prices and the North East Gas Grid are real, but the binding constraint - pipeline evacuation and B-80 well performance - is not improving), tam weak (a ~Rs 2,550 Cr E&P could 2-3x if capex executes, but the asset base and the sliding government revenue share cap the outcome well short of 10x/100x), moat no (commodity price-taker, no pricing power, evacuation-dependent), valuation no (~100x earnings at the 52-week high, ROCE 3.4%) -> score 1.0
The small/mid-cap live-inflection carve-out does NOT apply: there is no strong specific recent quarter (B-80 volumes are falling), only a multi-year capex promise with low credibility
Conviction Low: near debt-free and optionality on the gas grid keep it off the floor, but weak returns, a poor delivery record and a stretched multiple dominate
Seeded via oilfield-services / E&P theme (external lead, user-authorised bypass); value_chain block added (upstream producer, evacuation-gated)
No red flag tier (solvent, professionally managed, near debt-free)

four_box.note: moat no (commodity price-taker, evacuation-gated), valuation no (~100x P/E at 52-week high, ROCE 3.4%); tailwind and tam only weak because the crude/gas-grid optionality is real but the binding constraints (B-80 wells, Dirok pipeline) are not resolving and the sliding government revenue share caps upside.

value_chain.position: Upstream operator - owns and produces from discovered/producing hydrocarbon assets (Dirok gas, B-80 offshore oil & gas, PY-1/PY-3, Cambay). Sells crude to refiners via tanker offtake and gas to GSPC/regional buyers via ONGC terminals and the emerging North-East grid.
value_chain.pricing_power: None - price-taker on Brent-linked crude and formula-linked gas; a sliding government revenue share plus 10% royalty rises as revenue rises, structurally capping net realisations.
value_chain.key_inputs: Rig and well-services capex, offshore logistics (tankers, hoses), pipeline evacuation capacity (DNPL/DFL, North East Gas Grid).
value_chain.bottleneck: Pipeline evacuation for Dirok gas and well/offtake reliability for B-80 - the company is reportedly running at ~1/3 of capacity for want of evacuation.
